The present complaint has been filed by the complainant under section 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents, respondent no.1 is the husband and other respondents are the in laws of the complainant.
The brief facts of the case as have been disclosed in the complaint,
wherein,

Two children Master Mayank and Master Kartikeya were born out of this wedlock, who are now in the care and custody of the complainant.
It is stated that the father of the complainant had spent a huge amount and solemnized the marriage with great pomp and show.
The parents of the complainant gave numerous dowry articles to respondent no. 1 and his family members including furniture, jewelery articles of gold and silver etc in the marriage.

2. It is further stated that after the marriage, for some weeks everything went on well but after a few weeks, the respondent no. 2 & 3, who were in domestic relationship with the complainant, started harassing and torturing the complainant with one way or the other and continued to inflict the acts of domestic violence upon the complainant.

When the complainant was pregnant with first child ,
then the respondent no. 1 got her fallen from his moving motor bike intentionally and thus endangered the safety and life of the complainant and caused the domestic violence to her.
Thereafter the acts of the domestic violence were continuously inflicted upon the complainant by the respondent no.1, his mother, sister along with the respondent no. 2 & 3.

It is further stated that respondent no. 1 to 3 along with the mother and sister of the respondent no. 1 were not satisfied with the dowry articles which were given to them at the time of marriage with complainant.

sentences.text: I have heard Ld. Counsel for the parties and perused entire record with their assistance.

At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish, that firstly there is a domestic relationship as defined u/s 2(f) of the above said Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined u/s 3 of the said Act.

Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under :  CC No.

"domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have,
at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage,
adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
It is an admitted case of the parties that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the respondent no.1 on 12.12.2002 and out of the said wedlock, two children were born.
It is also an admitted case of the parties that they all resided together till 21122005.
Hence, the domestic relationship between the parties stands admitted.
14. It is also incumbent upon the complainant to establish that she has been a victim of domestic violence.

The complainant has deposed that that her parents had given had spent huge amount of Rs 10 Lacs and given sufficient dowry articles but the respondents were not satisfied and as such from the very beginning, they started harassing, beating and threatening her for bringing insufficient dowry and unless and until their demands were met, she would not live happily at their house and respondent no.1 would perform second marriage.
The respondent, his sister and mother commented "Tu Bhukhe Ghar ki Yahan Kaise Aa gayee".

She has further deposed that she informed her parents about the demands of the respondent and in laws then they along with other relatives tried to make the respondents understand but they could not succeed.
She was continuously subjected to very inhuman mental and physical torture, beatings and maltreatment by the respondents.
She was kept hungry to pressurize her to get fulfilled their demands and she was sent many times to her parental house.
15. She has further deposed that due to regular threats, harassment and beatings, her physical condition got worse but none cared to take pity upon her.
She has further deposed that she lived the life of a bonded labour at the matrimonial house.

The respondents used to scold her whenever she intended CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
to visit her parental house or to talk to her parents.

From the examination in chief of PW1/complainant, it is transpired that the complainant has leveled many allegations against her husband and in laws.

She has also mentioned some of the date of alleged incident against her mother in law as well as sister in law but strangely the complainant has not made them a party to this case for the reasons best known to her.

The allegations made in her examination in chief, appear to be mainly against her husband and she has not mentioned any thing specific against the respondent no.2 and 3, against whom only general and vague allegations have been made.
The complainant has not mentioned any specific, date, time and place, when the respondent no.2 and 3 had committed acts of domestic violence upon her.
The complainant has claimed to have been beaten mercilessly by the respondents several times but admittedly no complaint was ever made either by her or her parents and relatives before 21.12.2005.
The complainant had made complaint dated 21.12.2005 also against respondent no. 2 and 3 for assault but the said complaint has not been proved by the complainant in the present case.
During cross examination, the complainant has admitted that there is no mention of MLC dated 21.12.2005 in her affidavit.

During cross examination, she has admitted that she had filed a Civil Suit against her in laws to invoke her property rights and said suit has already been dismissed by concerned Ld.
Civil Judge.

During cross examination, she has further admitted that her elder sister in law was married 10 months before her marriage, which goes on to prove that her sister in law was residing at complainant's matrimonial house for being already married hence, the allegations of the complainant against her are false and incorrect.
The complainant has not deposed that her elder sister in law used to reside there only or used to visit her matrimonial house regularly.

19. The complainant has further admitted that a compromise had taken place between her and her husband at PS: Bhajanpura on 21.12.2005, which also goes on to suggest that the grievance of the complainant was mainly against her husband.

It be further observed that the respondent no.2 and 3 have been discharged in connected case of FIR No. 220/06, PS: Sarai Rohilla, under section 498 A/406/34 IPC vide order dated 15.12.2009 by Ld. Predecessor and said order was upheld even by the Hon'ble Appellate Court vide its order dated 19.05.2010.

In view thereof, the complainant has been unable to prove on record that she had been a victim of domestic violence at the hands of respondent no.2 and 3 and accordingly, they are discharged in the present case.
The complainant has however, been able to show on record that the respondent no.1 was committing acts of domestic violence upon her.
20. By way of present application, the complainant has prayed for protection order u/s 18 of the Act.

Admittedly, the complainant and her minor children are residing separately from the respondent and she has not narrated a single incident of violence since the day of separation, hence, no ground is made out for grant of protection order in the present case.

sentences.text: During cross examination, she has admitted that she has not filed any document to prove the ownership of the respondent with regard to said two buses and coaching center run by the respondent.

She has denied the suggestion that she has made false claims at para no.14 of her affidavit regarding the ownership of buses and coaching center run by her husband with sole intention to grab the property.
She has admitted that she has not filed any document with regard to ownership of immovable properties of her husband.

Though the complainant has not filed any document to prove the employment and income of the respondent but during cross examination, the respondent has not been able to negate her stand on the aspect of his own income and also failed to lead evidence in support of his claims.
25.

It is pertinent to mention here that while disposing of appeal of the complainant in connected case, Hon'ble Appellate court in its order dated 17.09.2012, has observed that during cross examination conducted on 11.01.2011 in connected case, the court finds that on substantial questions were put to the complainant with respect to her stand about financial status of the respondent.
The respondent has failed to lead evidence in support of his contentions or to rebut or controvert the averments of the complainant.
The Hon'ble Court has further observed that the respondent has admitted in his affidavit which he did not tender despite availing several opportunities.

He has admitted filing income tax returns but no such income tax returns were put on record leading to the clear presumption that the respondent has concealed material facts about his income from the court and in such circumstances, no concession could be given to the respondent and it had to be accepted that income suggested by the complainant was correct,
particularly when no questioning on this aspect was done during cross examination of the complainant.

The Hon'ble Court has further assessed the CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
income of respondent between Rs 15,000/ to 20,000/ per month and awarded total Rs 8,000/
per month as maintenance to the complainant as well as her children.

On the aspect of maintenance or monetary relief, this court feels that said order was passed way back on 17.09.2012 and since then there have been changes in circumstances.

The income of the respondent must have increased by now, whereas, the expenditure of the complainant must have also increased manifold on account of high price rises, costly living standard, education expenses of growing children etc., accordingly, the maintenance amount awarded to the complainant and her children also deserves to be enhanced.

Having regard to status of the parties, their responsibilities,
the respondent is directed to make arrangement for Rs. 15,000/ ( Rs Fifteen Thousand) per month in favour of complainant and minor children from the date of filing of present petition.
Payment shall be made or be deposited in bank account of complainant by 10th of every month.
Maintenance awarded in any other proceedings shall be liable to adjustment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The present complaint has been filed by the complainant under section 12 of Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the respondents, respondent no.1 is the husband and other respondents are the in laws of the complainant.
The respondent no. 1 CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma &
Ors.
used to beat the complainant on one pretext or the other.
The respondent no. 1 ignored his matrimonial obligations and turned a deaf ear from the complainant.
On 21.12.2005, police personnel of PS Bhajanpura got a compromise effected between the parties, but in defiance of the compromise , no body from the respondent side including the respondent no. 1 came to bring her back to matrimonial house/shared household rather the complainant when visited herself along with her brother to the matrimonial house, she was beaten mercilessly by the respondent no. 1 & 2 along with her mother in law and sister in law.
While the complainant is presently residing at her parental house and is a burden upon her parents and has no shelter and is deprived of her economic status along with her two minor children due to the acts and omission of domestic violence of the respondents.
Reply has been filed by the respondents wherein they have stated that the Domestic violence Act, 2005 is only prospective in operation and not retrospective in operation.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Ld. Counsel for respondent no.2 and 3 have placed reliance upon the judgment of RENU MITTAL Vs ANIL MITTAL & ORS , DOD:27.09.2010 & SR BATRA Vs TARUNA BATRA,
DOD: 15.12.2006 13.
In view thereof, the complainant has been unable to prove on record that she had been a victim of domestic violence at the hands of respondent no.2 and 3 and accordingly, they are discharged in the present case.
The complainant has prayed for providing reasonable accommodation in any of CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs.
Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
the two houses owned by the respondents, restraining them to dispossess them from said shared household, alienating or disposing of the shared household or encumbering the same and restraining the respondents from renouncing their rights in the shared household without prior permission.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
At the very outset, it is pertinent to mention that complainant in order to be entitled to the relief under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is required to establish, that firstly there is a domestic relationship as defined u/s 2(f) of the above said Act between complainant and respondents and thereafter it is also required to be established that she has been a victim of domestic violence as defined u/s 3 of the said Act.
Domestic relationship has been defined under the Act in Section 2(f) as under :  CC No.
49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
"domestic relationship" means a relationship between two persons who live or have,
at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage,
adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
It is an admitted case of the parties that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the respondent no.1 on 12.12.2002 and out of the said wedlock, two children were born.
The complainant has however, been able to show on record that the respondent no.1 was committing acts of domestic violence upon her.
20. By way of present application, the complainant has prayed for protection order u/s 18 of the Act.
Admittedly, the complainant and her minor children are residing separately from the respondent and she has not narrated a single incident of violence since the day of separation, hence, no ground is made out for grant of protection order in the present case.
21.
Residence order u/s 19 of the Act has also been claimed.
In this regard, it be observed that the competent Civil Court has already decided the claims of the parties and held that properties in question exclusively belong to respondent no. 2 and the complainant has no right therein whatsoever.
Hence, the complainant is not entitled to residence order as claimed above.
On the other hand, the respondent no. 1 has denied the claims of the complainant with regard to his employment and income.
24. In this regard, it be observed that the complainant has not filed any CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
document with regard to employment and income of the respondent.
The respondent has failed to lead evidence in support of his contentions or to rebut or controvert the averments of the complainant.
He has admitted filing income tax returns but no such income tax returns were put on record leading to the clear presumption that the respondent has concealed material facts about his income from the court and in such circumstances, no concession could be given to the respondent and it had to be accepted that income suggested by the complainant was correct,
particularly when no questioning on this aspect was done during cross examination of the complainant.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The Hon'ble Court has further assessed the CC No. 49/1/08 PS: Sarai Rohilla Seema Sharma Vs. Krishan Kumar Sharma & Ors.
income of respondent between Rs 15,000/ to 20,000/ per month and awarded total Rs 8,000/
per month as maintenance to the complainant as well as her children.

9 26.
On the aspect of maintenance or monetary relief, this court feels that said order was passed way back on 17.09.2012 and since then there have been changes in circumstances.
The income of the respondent must have increased by now, whereas, the expenditure of the complainant must have also increased manifold on account of high price rises, costly living standard, education expenses of growing children etc., accordingly, the maintenance amount awarded to the complainant and her children also deserves to be enhanced.
Having regard to status of the parties, their responsibilities,
the respondent is directed to make arrangement for Rs. 15,000/ ( Rs Fifteen Thousand) per month in favour of complainant and minor children from the date of filing of present petition.
Payment shall be made or be deposited in bank account of complainant by 10th of every month.
Maintenance awarded in any other proceedings shall be liable to adjustment.
27. File be consigned to Record Room.
ANNOUNCED IN OPEN COURT
Present : None for the parties
Vide separate detailed order, the present petition is disposed off.
